summary.text: The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of flattened sacs and tubes enclosed by membrane, found in most eukaryotic cells as part of their transportation system.
Rough ER is studded with ribosomes that make proteins, while smooth ER lacks ribosomes and works in lipid synthesis, steroid hormone production and detoxification.
Its membranes are continuous with the outer nuclear membrane, and membrane-bound vesicles shuttle proteins from it to the Golgi apparatus.

facts.label: Name meaning
facts.value: 'Within the cytoplasm' plus Latin for 'little net'

facts.label: Two types
facts.value: Rough endoplasmic reticulum and smooth endoplasmic reticulum

items.prompt: A cell is specialised for making steroid hormones. Which type of ER should it contain a lot of?

options.label: Smooth ER, which lacks ribosomes
Rough ER, because hormone making needs ribosomes on the surface
Neither, since hormones are made outside the ER
Rough ER, because it is the only type that makes lipids

items.explain: Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and produces steroid hormones, and cells hold different ratios of the two types depending on their activities.

items.prompt: Under an electron microscope one ER surface looks bumpy. What causes the bumps?

options.label: Golgi vesicles stacked on its inner face
Nuclear pores built into its sheets
Ribosomes attached to its outer face
Crystals of cholesterol in its membrane

items.explain: The outer face of rough ER is studded with ribosomes, which gives it a rough appearance.

items.prompt: A free ribosome starts translating the mRNA of a protein destined for secretion. What gets it to the ER?

options.label: It was a permanent part of the ER from the start and never moves
The first amino acids form a signal peptide that a signal recognition particle binds
A COPII vesicle carries the ribosome over from the Golgi
A mannose-6-phosphate tag added in the Golgi guides it

items.explain: The first amino acids encode a signal peptide recognized by a signal recognition particle, which brings the ribosome to the RER translocon.

items.prompt: No membrane runs unbroken between the ER and the Golgi apparatus. How do new proteins travel between them?

options.label: Through nuclear pores that join the two compartments
Carried by ribosomes that move along the cytoskeleton
Through tubes of smooth ER that fuse with the Golgi
In membrane-bound transport vesicles that shuttle between the two

items.explain: Although the two are not joined by a continuous membrane, membrane-bound transport vesicles shuttle proteins between them.

items.prompt: The gap between the two membranes of the nuclear envelope is connected to the inside of another structure. Which one?

options.label: The matrix of a mitochondrion
The lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum
The cytosol around the organelles
The nucleolus inside the nucleus

items.explain: The perinuclear space between the two nuclear membranes is continuous with the ER lumen.

items.prompt: A cell's activities change over time. What can happen to its ER?

options.label: Rough and smooth ER amounts can slowly interchange
Nothing, since rough ER always stays rough
The ER is shed and the Golgi takes over its work
Smooth ER turns into ribosomes

items.explain: The quantity of rough and smooth ER can slowly interchange depending on the cell's changing metabolic activities.
